newsitem.title: TAIWAN: POLL-TAIWAN 2ND-QTR GDP GROWTH SEEN UP 5.81 PCT.
newsitem.headline: POLL-TAIWAN 2ND-QTR GDP GROWTH SEEN UP 5.81 PCT.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Wednesday projected a 5.81 percent in year-on-year growth for Taiwan's Gross Domestic Product in the second quarter of 1997.
Official figures were to be released by the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics around 0900 GMT on August 15.
The first-quarter GDP rose 6.83 percent year-on-year.

The 5.81 percent forecast was higher than the statistics directorate's May forecast of 5.61 percent.
Economists attributed their relatively higher forecast to smaller-than-expected impact of a hog disease and strong stock market performance in the second quarter.

"After the government's persistent efforts to help solve the problem, the hog epidemic's actual impact turned out to be not as serious as originally had expected," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.

Officials had estimated the outbreak of the hog foot-and-mouth disease on March 20, which resulted an overall cut off of the island's pork exports, would reduce Taiwan's GDP growth by between 0.39 and 0.50 percentage point.

"The stock market performance was also much better than expected, boosting output in service and financial industries as well as in private consumption," said International Investment Trust economist Hung Chao-lung.
The stock index rose some 13 percent in the second quarter to close in end-June at 9,030.28 points. It surged some 30 percent in the first half.
